addExplainers.title: A photo from long ago
addExplainers.body:
Ask your grown-up for one old photo, or one old thing that belongs to your family. Look at it together.

Who is in the photo? What is it? Point to it and talk about it with your grown-up. A photo or an old thing can tell you about your family, just like a book tells you about a story.

Say one thing you found out from looking at it.
bullets: Point to the photo or the old thing.
Ask your grown-up: what is this, and who is in it?
Say one thing you learned from looking at it.

addExplainers.title: Ask two people in your family
addExplainers.body:
Ask two grown-ups in your family the very same question: what was your favourite game when you were little?

Listen carefully to each answer. Did they say the same game, or a different one?

Everyone in your family knows different things, because they have lived different lives. That is why it is worth asking more than one person.
bullets: Ask the first grown-up your question. Listen.
Ask the second grown-up the same question. Listen.
Say what each person told you.
